fixed.q: Which machine recognises regular languages?
fixed.w: Regular: FA; context-free: PDA; context-sensitive: LBA; recursively enumerable: Turing machine.

fixed.q: Compared with DFAs, NFAs:
fixed.w: Subset construction converts an n-state NFA to a DFA with at most 2ⁿ states.

fixed.q: The minimum number of states in a DFA accepting binary strings whose number of 1s is divisible by 3 is:
fixed.w: Track the count mod 3. Strings divisible by n (as numbers) need n states (for n not a power of 2, generally).

fixed.q: A DFA accepting all binary strings that end with '01' needs at least how many states?
fixed.w: Strings ending with a k-length pattern need k + 1 states.

fixed.q: Which language is NOT regular?
fixed.w: aⁿbⁿ needs counting (it is context-free). Proved non-regular with the pumping lemma.

fixed.q: Regular languages are closed under:
o: Union, intersection, complement, concatenation and Kleene star
fixed.w: CFLs are closed under union, concatenation, star but NOT intersection or complement.

fixed.q: The regular expression (a + b)* denotes:
o: All strings over {a, b} including ε
Only strings with equal a and b
fixed.w: (a + b)+ excludes ε.

fixed.q: The pumping lemma is used to prove that a language is:
Context-free languages are recognised by:
fixed.w: A PDA = FA + one stack. Two stacks = Turing machine power. DPDA is less powerful than NPDA.

fixed.q: A grammar is ambiguous if some string has:
o: More than one parse tree (or leftmost derivation)
fixed.w: Ambiguity is undecidable in general.

fixed.q: In Chomsky Normal Form, every production is of the form:
fixed.w: Greibach Normal Form: A → aα.

fixed.q: Which is the correct Chomsky hierarchy (most to least restrictive)?
o: Type 3 regular ⊂ Type 2 CFL ⊂ Type 1 CSL ⊂ Type 0 RE
fixed.w: Type 0 unrestricted (Turing machine), Type 1 context-sensitive (LBA), Type 2 context-free (PDA), Type 3 regular (FA).

fixed.q: Which problem is undecidable?
o: Whether a DFA accepts a given string
fixed.w: Also undecidable: CFG ambiguity, equivalence of two CFGs, Post correspondence problem.

fixed.q: A language accepted by a Turing machine that always halts is called:
fixed.w: Recursive ⊂ recursively enumerable. The complement of a recursive language is recursive.

fixed.q: Compared with a deterministic Turing machine, a non-deterministic TM:
fixed.w: Church–Turing thesis: TMs capture effective computability.

fixed.q: In a Moore machine the output depends on ___, and in a Mealy machine on ___.
o: the present state only; the present state and input
the input only; the state only
the state and input; the state only
fixed.w: For the same input of length n, Moore gives n + 1 outputs, Mealy n.

fixed.q: How many strings of length 3 are there over the alphabet {a, b}?
Which regular expression gives all binary strings with at least one 1?
Which language is context-sensitive but not context-free?
fixed.w: wwᴿ (palindromes) is context-free.

fixed.q: Which is NOT closed under intersection?
fixed.w: CFL ∩ regular is context-free, though.

fixed.q: Which is the correct order of compiler phases?
o: Lexical analysis, syntax analysis, semantic analysis, intermediate code, optimisation, code generation
Syntax, lexical, semantic, code generation, optimisation
Lexical, semantic, syntax, optimisation, code generation
fixed.w: Front end: lexical, syntax, semantic, intermediate code. Back end: optimisation, code generation. Symbol table used throughout.

fixed.q: Which compiler phase produces tokens?
fixed.w: Uses regular expressions / finite automata. Tools: Lex/Flex. Parser generator: Yacc/Bison.

fixed.q: Type checking is done during:
fixed.w: The semantic analyser gathers type information into the syntax tree / symbol table.

fixed.q: Which data structure stores information about identifiers (names, types, scope)?
The number of tokens in: int a = b + 10; is:
Which translator executes a program line by line without producing an object file?
fixed.w: Compiler translates the whole program; assembler converts assembly to machine code; loader puts the executable in memory; linker combines object files.

fixed.q: Which parser is top-down?
fixed.w: Bottom-up (shift-reduce) parsers trace a rightmost derivation in reverse.

fixed.q: Which grammar property must be removed before top-down (LL) parsing?
fixed.w: Also left-factor the grammar.

fixed.q: Order the LR parsers by power:
fixed.w: SLR and LALR have the same number of states (LR(0) items); CLR has the most. YACC builds LALR(1).

fixed.q: Shift-reduce parsing corresponds to:
o: The reverse of a rightmost derivation
fixed.w: Conflicts possible: shift-reduce and reduce-reduce (not shift-shift).

fixed.q: Which conflicts can occur in LR parsing?
FIRST(S) for S → aA | bB, A → c, B → d is:
fixed.w: FIRST collects the terminals that can begin strings derived from S.

fixed.q: A synthesized attribute gets its value from:
o: The attributes of its children in the parse tree
fixed.w: Inherited attributes come from parent/siblings. S-attributed definitions suit bottom-up (LR) parsing.

fixed.q: Which is a common intermediate representation?
fixed.w: Representations: quadruples, triples, indirect triples, syntax trees, DAGs, postfix.

fixed.q: Replacing 3 * 4 with 12 at compile time is:
fixed.w: Strength reduction: replace x*2 with x+x or a shift. Code motion: move loop-invariant code out of loops.

fixed.q: Peephole optimisation is a:
o: Local optimisation over a small window of instructions
fixed.w: Removes redundant loads/stores, unreachable code, applies algebraic simplification.

fixed.q: Some optimisations are done on intermediate code because it:
o: Makes the compiler easier to port to other target machines

fixed.q: Activation records for function calls are kept on the:
fixed.w: Heap holds dynamically allocated data.

fixed.q: A basic block is:
o: A sequence of statements with one entry and one exit and no branches in between
fixed.w: Leaders: first statement, targets of jumps, statements after jumps.

fixed.q: Which program places an executable program in main memory ready for execution?
fixed.w: The SSC 2017 paper asked this.

fixed.q: Which of the following statement(s) is/are correct regarding Assembly language? I. An assembler converts (or assembles) the symbolic program of an Assembly language into its equivalent machine program. II. A program written in an assembly language is machine dependent.
fixed.w: An assembler translates symbolic code to machine code, and assembly language is machine-dependent. Both statements are true.

fixed.q: Which of the given options best describes the truthfulness of the following statements? i) Assembly languages are machine dependent. ii) A compiler is a program which produces a machine-level program from the specifications of a high-level language. iii) An interpreter translates and executes each program statement, one at a time. iv) 'BASIC' language is an interactive programming language.
fixed.w: All four statements are true: assembly is machine-dependent, a compiler produces machine code, an interpreter runs one statement at a time, and BASIC is interactive.

fixed.q: ______ is a system software package that converts a high level language program to machine language.
fixed.w: A compiler translates a whole high-level program into machine language.

fixed.q: A ____ file is a sequence of bytes organised into blocks understandable by the system's linker.
fixed.w: Object files are the linker's input.

fixed.q: Which of the following is the purpose of the ORIGIN directive?
o: To indicate the starting position in memory where the program block is to be stored.
To indicate the start of the computation code.
To indicate the purpose of the code.
To list the locations of all registers used.
fixed.w: ORIGIN (ORG) sets the starting memory address where the following code or data is placed.

fixed.q: Which directive is used to perform initialisation before the code is executed?
fixed.w: DATAWORD initialises memory locations with given values. RESERVE only sets space aside, and EQU defines a constant name.

fixed.q: Which of the following should be the last statement of a source program?
fixed.w: The END directive tells the assembler that the source program has finished.

fixed.q: Which of the following statements is true?
o: When dealing with branching code, the assembler finds the branch offset and replaces the branch target with it.
When dealing with branching code, the assembler replaces the target with its address.
When dealing with branching code, the assembler does not replace until the test condition is satisfied.
When dealing with branching code, the assembler replaces the target with the value given by the DATAWORD instruction.
fixed.w: For relative branches the assembler computes the offset from the current location to the target label and puts that offset in the instruction.

fixed.q: Which of the following does the assembler use to store all names and their related values?
fixed.w: The symbol table maps labels and names to their addresses or values.

fixed.q: Assume that the SLR parser for a grammar G has n1 states and the LALR parser for G has n2 states. The relationship between n1 and n2 is:
o: n1 is necessarily less than n2
n1 is necessarily equal to n2
n1 is necessarily greater than n2
fixed.w: SLR and LALR are both built on the LR(0) item sets (LALR merges LR(1) states with the same core), so they always have the same number of states.

fixed.q: The types of conflicts that can arise in LR(0) techniques are ____.
fixed.w: LR parsers can have shift-reduce and reduce-reduce conflicts. A shift-shift conflict cannot happen, so A is the only valid choice here.

fixed.q: The LL(1) and LR(0) techniques are ____.
o: Both simulate reverse of rightmost derivation
Both simulate reverse of leftmost derivation
fixed.w: Some grammars are LL(1) but not LR(0), and the reverse is also true, so the classes are incomparable.

fixed.q: Consider an ε-free CFG. If for every pair of productions A → u and A → v:
o: If FIRST(u) ∩ FIRST(v) is empty then the CFG has to be LL(1)
If the CFG is LL(1) then FIRST(u) ∩ FIRST(v) has to be empty
fixed.w: Without ε-productions, FOLLOW sets don't matter, so disjoint FIRST sets for every pair of alternatives is both necessary and sufficient for LL(1) (GATE 2007).

fixed.q: Which of the following phase of the compiler, gathers type information and saves it in either the syntax tree or the symbol table, for subsequent use during intermediate code generation?
fixed.w: The semantic analyser does type checking and records type information in the syntax tree or symbol table for intermediate code generation.

fixed.q: Which of the following is a translator that translates source code into object (target) code?
fixed.w: A compiler translates source code into object (target) code.

fixed.q: Which one of the following statements is FALSE?
o: Context-free grammar can be used to specify both lexical and syntax rules.
Type checking is done before parsing.
High-level language programs can be translated to different intermediate representations.
Arguments to a function can be passed using the program stack.
fixed.w: Type checking is part of semantic analysis, which happens after parsing (GATE 2018).

fixed.q: The number of tokens in the following C/C++ statement is: printf("i=%d, &i=%xx", i&i);
fixed.w: Printf, (, the string literal, comma, i, &, i, ), and ; make 9 tokens.

fixed.q: Some code optimizations are carried out on the intermediate code because:
o: they enhance the portability of the compiler to other target processors
program analysis is more accurate on intermediate code than on machine code
the information from data flow analysis cannot otherwise be used for optimization
the information from the front end cannot otherwise be used for optimization
fixed.w: Optimising machine-independent intermediate code means the optimiser can be reused for every target, which makes the compiler more portable (GATE 2008).

fixed.q: A synthesized attribute can easily be simulated by an
fixed.w: Synthesized attributes are computed at reductions, which LR (bottom-up) parsers do naturally.

fixed.q: Which of the following problems is not NP-complete but undecidable?
fixed.w: The halting problem is undecidable. Partition, Hamiltonian circuit and bin packing are decidable NP-complete problems.

fixed.q: A language L for which there exists a TM 'T' that accepts every word in L and either rejects or loops for every word that is not in L is said to be
fixed.w: Accept-on-yes but possibly loop-on-no is exactly recursively enumerable. Recursive languages need a TM that always halts.

fixed.q: Choose the correct statements.
o: A total recursive function is also a partial recursive function.
A partial recursive function is also a total recursive function.
A partial recursive function is also a primitive recursive function.
fixed.w: Total recursive functions are a subset of partial recursive functions. The reverse inclusions don't hold.

fixed.q: The logic of the pumping lemma is a good example of
fixed.w: A string longer than the number of DFA states must revisit some state (pigeonhole), which creates the loop that can be pumped.

fixed.q:
Which of the following definitions generates the same language as L, where L = {xⁿyⁿ, n ≥ 1}?
i. E → xEy | xy

ii. xy | x⁺xyy⁺

iii. x⁺y⁺
fixed.w: Only the grammar in (i) forces equal counts. The regular expressions in (ii) and (iii) can't match counts of x and y.

theory.Automata:
• FA ↔ regular; PDA ↔ context-free; LBA ↔ context-sensitive; TM ↔ recursively enumerable.
• NFA = DFA in power (subset construction, ≤ 2ⁿ states).
• DFA for strings ending in a k-length pattern: k + 1 states; count of 1s mod m: m states.
• Moore output depends on state; Mealy on state + input.
theory.Regular languages:
• Closed under union, intersection, complement, concatenation, star. aⁿbⁿ is not regular (pumping lemma).
• (a + b)* includes ε; (a + b)+ doesn't. |Σ|ⁿ strings of length n.
theory.CFG & PDA:
• Ambiguous = two parse trees for a string. CNF: A → BC | a. GNF: A → aα.
• CFLs closed under union, concatenation, star; not intersection or complement. DPDA < NPDA.
theory.Chomsky hierarchy: • Type 3 regular ⊂ Type 2 CF ⊂ Type 1 CS ⊂ Type 0 RE. aⁿbⁿcⁿ is context-sensitive, not CF.
theory.Turing machines: • Halting problem undecidable; also CFG ambiguity, CFG equivalence, PCP. Recursive (always halts) ⊂ RE. NTM = DTM in power.
theory.Phases:
• Lexical (tokens; Lex) → syntax (parse tree; Yacc) → semantic (type checking) → intermediate code → optimisation → code generation. Symbol table throughout.
• Count tokens: keywords, identifiers, operators, constants, punctuation each count once.
theory.Translators: • Compiler: whole program. Interpreter: line by line. Assembler: assembly → machine. Linker: joins object files. Loader: places executable in memory.
theory.Parsing:
• Top-down: recursive descent, LL(1) — remove left recursion, left-factor. Bottom-up (shift-reduce): reverse of rightmost derivation.
• Power: LR(0) < SLR(1) < LALR(1) < CLR(1); SLR and LALR have the same number of states. YACC = LALR(1). Conflicts: shift-reduce, reduce-reduce.
• FIRST(X): terminals that can start X.
theory.SDT: • Synthesized attributes from children (S-attributed, bottom-up). Inherited from parent/siblings (L-attributed).
theory.Intermediate code: • Three-address code (quadruples, triples, indirect triples), syntax trees, DAGs, postfix. Optimising on IR aids portability.
theory.Optimisation: • Constant folding, constant propagation, common subexpression elimination, dead-code elimination, code motion (loop-invariant), strength reduction, loop unrolling. Peephole = local, small window.
theory.Runtime: • Activation records on the stack; dynamic data on the heap.
theory.Code generation: • Basic block: one entry, one exit. Leaders: first statement, jump targets, statements after jumps. Register allocation, instruction selection.
theory.System software:
• Assembler: assembly → machine code. Two-pass assembler: pass 1 builds the symbol table (location counter), pass 2 generates code.
• Linker: combines object modules and libraries, resolving external references. Loader: places the program in memory for execution; relocating loader adjusts addresses.
• Macro processor expands macros (no call overhead, unlike subroutines).
• Compiler vs interpreter; cross compiler (code for another machine); bootstrapping.
• Absolute loader → no relocation; dynamic linking → at run time (DLLs).
